## Narrative

The metabolomics data point to a profound disruption of **Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG hsa00260)** as the dominant signal, with an FDR of 0.0 and an extraordinary fold-enrichment of 568.9 — the strongest candidate by several orders of magnitude. Six input metabolites map to this pathway: L-Methionine (C00073), L-Cysteine (C00097), S-Adenosylhomocysteine (C00021), Ornithine (C00077), 2-Ketobutyric acid (C00109), and (R)-Lipoic acid (C16241). A secondary enrichment in **Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives (Reactome R-HSA-71291)** reinforces that amino-acid interconversion is broadly affected.

The methionine–cysteine axis is the clearest driver. Within the methionine cycle, L-Methionine (C00073) is metabolised to S-Adenosylmethionine, which donates its methyl group to diverse acceptors and is then recycled to S-Adenosylhomocysteine (C00021). The KEGG reaction graph confirms this two-step flow (Methionine → S-Adenosylmethionine → S-Adenosylhomocysteine). Accumulation of S-Adenosylhomocysteine — a potent inhibitor of S-Adenosylmethionine-dependent methyltransferases — suggests impaired methylation capacity, consistent with disrupted one-carbon metabolism. L-Cysteine (C00097), which feeds into this cycle via trans-sulfuration, reinforces the centrality of this hub.

The **ornithine–proline branch** is also implicated. Ornithine (C00077) is connected to 1-Pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid (C03912) — an intermediate in both arginine and proline catabolism — via a three-step KEGG path through glutamate and arginine. Elevated ornithine alongside 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid could reflect increased flux through arginase and proline oxidase activities, potentially indicating heightened demand for ornithine-derived polyamines or proline for collagen synthesis.

Biologically, these changes implicate **one-carbon metabolism and redox homeostasis**. Lipoic acid (C16241) and 2-ketobutyric acid (C00109) further anchor the network in oxidative metabolism. S-Adenosylhomocysteine accumulation is a hallmark of disrupted methylation, which affects DNA, proteins, and phospholipids, and is observed in liver disease, cardiovascular pathology, and neurological disorders. Meanwhile, ornithine dysregulation is linked to urea cycle disorders and altered neurotransmitter synthesis. The simultaneous perturbation of these nodes — driven by methionine/cysteine depletion and ornithine excess — is consistent with a metabolic shift toward oxidative stress and impaired methyl donor regeneration.
